answer: Each claim must carry jade ballast: a weight carved only when three strangers each verify one distinct job, and the carving cannot be copied. Every identity is a vertex in the trust graph, and payout flows only to vertices triangulated by three independent stranger edges, the same three carvers. Ballasted claims sink into the ocean current that carries payouts forward; unballasted claims drift and strand. Clones from one operator share edges, so n vertices collapse into one and split a single payout, while each clone still paid for its own ballast; per-clone pay falls as 1/n.
